subject: Agriculture
title: Plant-Based Meat
description: A micro-lesson that makes Plant-Based Meat usable.

hook.text: The Impossible Burger bleeds like meat, sizzles like meat, and uses 96% less land. It's made from plants.

buildup.text: Heme—an iron-containing molecule found in blood—gives meat its flavor. Impossible Foods makes it from soy roots.

discovery.text: Plant-based meat produces 90% less greenhouse gas and uses 46% less energy than conventional beef.

twist.text: Sales plateaued after initial hype. Many consumers tried plant meat once and returned to animal meat.

climax.text: If plant-based meat reaches taste and price parity with animal meat, the market could shift rapidly.

punchline.text: Same taste, 90% less damage. The barrier isn't technology—it's habit.

quiz.question: How does the Impossible Burger replicate the taste of meat?
options: Using heme produced from soy roots, the same molecule that gives blood its flavor
